title: Time zones follow the session; gaps and overlaps resolve inconsistently
verdict: `CONVERT_TIMEZONE` moves a gap forward, a `TIMESTAMP_LTZ` cast backward; overlaps take the earlier instant
description: `TIMESTAMP_LTZ` reads and prints in the session's `TIMEZONE`. In New York's gap, `CONVERT_TIMEZONE('America/New_York', 'UTC', '2024-03-10 02:30:00')` is `07:30` UTC (03:30 EDT, forward), but `'2024-03-10 02:30:00'::TIMESTAMP_LTZ` under that session zone is `01:30 -05:00` (backward). In the overlap, both take the earlier instant (`01:30 -04:00`, `05:30` UTC).
`TIMESTAMP_TZ` values compare as instants. `DATEADD(DAY, 1, …)` keeps the wall-clock time across a DST change (`TIMESTAMP_DAY_IS_ALWAYS_24H` is false).
reference: Time zones are outside the model: sverify's SQL writes `TIMESTAMP_NTZ` only, which no session parameter changes.

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)
provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
